acceptance.assertion: A regression simulates deploy generation N upgrading to N+1 where N+1 changes the deploy verifier/runtime contract; the upgrade completes autonomously without manually replacing the installed deploy executable.
Staging the next deploy generation remains exact-head/hash/preimage bound, rejects unsafe path identity or unexpected bytes fail-closed, and preserves rollback semantics when target validation fails.
After successful N→N+1 convergence, an unchanged second deploy creates no release, performs no unnecessary service restart, and reports the same exact runtime head.

A controlled live acceptance on the Heim-PC proves automatic convergence from a deliberately older compatible deploy generation to the reviewed next generation and leaves the deploy timer, UI, and remote bridge healthy.

approval.note: Repository and deployment-path hardening only; preserve current fail-closed verifier, hash/preimage binding, rollback, and service gates.

goal: Make Audiozentrale's self-deploy path capable of safely advancing from deploy generation N to N+1 even when the next release changes verifier/runtime contracts, without a manual bootstrap and without weakening fail-closed rollback or identity checks.

metadata.discovery: Post-merge runtime verification of audio PR #89 exposed a self-deploy bootstrap deadlock: the old installed deploy verifier expected 7 remote effects, rejected the new correct 10-effect bridge contract, and rolled back every minute. PR #90 fixed the immediate allowlist drift and added parity CI, but escaping the already-installed old generation still required one controlled hash-bound bootstrap.
does_not_establish: A need to weaken runtime verification
Permission to bypass reviewed deploy generations

title: Make Audiozentrale self-deploy bootstrap-safe across deploy-contract changes
